generation_system: Follow the writing request. Return only the requested content.

prompts.text: Explain thermal expansion to a caretaker fitting a copper pipe across a fictional greenhouse named Rill House. Use a concrete example involving a 6-metre pipe. Aim for about 80 whitespace-separated words in total.

Explain how a checksum detects an accidental change in a list of parcel weights at fictional depot Sable Quay. Include a small numerical example and a limitation. Aim for about 180 whitespace-separated words in total.

Explain why a rotating compost bin can warm up to a new volunteer at the fictional Alder Foot allotment. Distinguish the source of heat from the role of turning. Aim for about 450 whitespace-separated words in total.

Describe why a siphon moves water between two tanks at fictional Mossgate workshop. Use the relative tank heights and explain when the flow stops. Aim for about 180 whitespace-separated words in total.

Teach a novice at fictional Bracken Observatory how parallax estimates distance. Use two viewing positions, a nearby marker and a distant ridge, with a numerical example. Aim for about 450 whitespace-separated words in total.

Summarise this fictional notice for a resident: Torren Library will close its north room for six days starting 8 November. The south reading room stays open. Book returns move to the garden gate. The repair budget is 7400 credits. A volunteer session was proposed but not approved. Aim for about 80 whitespace-separated words in total.

Summarise this fictional trial: Fen Workshop compared two packaging inserts on 84 glass jars. Insert A was used on 42 and 5 arrived cracked; B was used on 42 and 3 cracked. Delivery routes differed. B cost 0.14 credits more per jar. The manager requested a second trial before changing suppliers. Aim for about 180 whitespace-separated words in total.

Summarise this fictional committee record: Marlow Marsh counted 213 reed beds in spring and 201 in autumn. Two surveyors used different maps. The west footpath was closed for 19 days after flooding. An 1800-credit boardwalk was approved by 6 votes to 3. No decision was taken on fencing. Residents asked for another bird count. Aim for about 450 whitespace-separated words in total.

Condense this fictional service report for customers: Lumen Ferry ran 168 scheduled crossings in June. It cancelled 9 for wind and 3 for maintenance. A replacement timetable starts 11 July, adding a 07:40 trip on Tuesdays. Tickets retain their price of 6 credits. The operator has not decided whether to add weekend trips. Aim for about 180 whitespace-separated words in total.

Write a structured summary of this fictional pilot for a club chair: Pell Community Hall lent 48 repair kits during a ten-week trial. Thirty-four came back within seven days, 9 came back later and 5 remained outstanding at the cutoff. Users paid a refundable 12-credit deposit. Staff logged 17 requests for instructions in larger print. The trial used 620 credits, excluding staff time. Only 22 users completed a survey; 18 of them would borrow again. A proposal to double the stock was deferred until the missing kits are followed up. Aim for about 450 whitespace-separated words in total.

Write an email from a fictional pottery tutor to a learner, rescheduling a lesson from 14:00 Friday to 10:30 Saturday because the kiln is being serviced. Offer a refund if Saturday is unsuitable. Aim for about 80 whitespace-separated words in total.

Write a calm email from fictional shop Merrow Cycles to a supplier. The order for 16 green lamps contained 11 green and 5 blue. Ask for a replacement plan by Wednesday, without assuming who caused the error. Aim for about 180 whitespace-separated words in total.

Write an email from a fictional neighbourhood choir coordinator to members about moving rehearsals from Cedar Room to Rowan Room for three weeks. Explain the temporary seating plan, step-free access and where to send clashes. Do not invent dates or contact details. Aim for about 450 whitespace-separated words in total.

Draft an email from fictional community garden East Wren to a tool-hire shop. A booked cultivator arrived with a broken handle. Describe the effect on the Saturday work session, request repair or replacement, and ask how to return it. Aim for about 180 whitespace-separated words in total.

Write an email from the fictional Pellin Museum volunteer lead to new guides. A trial route now starts in the map room instead of the courtyard, lasts 35 minutes and has two seated stops. Explain how to help visitors who arrive late, how to record questions the guide cannot answer, and how to send feedback after the first tour. Keep it welcoming and specific; do not invent addresses or policies. Aim for about 450 whitespace-separated words in total.

Write Python function longest_plateau(values) returning the length of the longest run of equal consecutive values. Empty input returns 0. Include a docstring and two examples. Aim for about 80 whitespace-separated words in total.

Write Python function combine_counts(pairs) accepting (label, count) pairs and returning sums by label in first-seen order. Reject negative counts with ValueError. Include tests as examples, without external libraries. Aim for about 180 whitespace-separated words in total.

Write Python function collapse_windows(windows) merging overlapping or touching integer (start,end) intervals. Reject end<start, preserve the input and return sorted tuples. Explain the algorithm and include edge-case examples. Use only the standard library. Aim for about 450 whitespace-separated words in total.

Implement Python function stable_unique_last(items): keep the final occurrence of each hashable value while preserving the order of those retained positions. Include a docstring and examples for empty input and repeated values. Do not execute the code. Aim for about 180 whitespace-separated words in total.

Write Python function allocate_slots(requests, capacity), where requests is a sequence of positive integer sizes. Greedily accept a request if it fits remaining capacity, otherwise reject it; do not reorder. Return accepted indices and remaining capacity. Validate nonnegative integer capacity and positive integer sizes, rejecting booleans too. Include examples, edge cases, and a short complexity explanation using only the standard library. Aim for about 450 whitespace-separated words in total.

Give a reasoned opinion for a fictional village club on whether to replace a monthly printed notice with a phone message group. Consider members without smartphones and suggest a practical decision. Aim for about 80 whitespace-separated words in total.

Advise a fictional repair cafe deciding between walk-in queues and reserved appointments. Its volunteers are few and some repairs take much longer than others. Explain a tradeoff and choose an approach. Aim for about 180 whitespace-separated words in total.

Give an opinion on whether a fictional college workshop should lend specialist tools for home projects. Consider training, access and lost equipment. State a decision and a condition that would change it. Aim for about 450 whitespace-separated words in total.

Recommend whether a fictional reading club should choose its next book by a public vote or a rotating member choice. Some members read slowly and the club has twelve regulars. Explain your reasoning. Aim for about 180 whitespace-separated words in total.

Argue for a decision by fictional canal group Beryl Lock on whether to allow booked evening visits. Volunteers currently open only two afternoons a week, neighbours are concerned about noise, and an evening pilot would need lighting. Discuss the strongest objection to your preferred option and propose a way to judge a six-week trial, without inventing survey results. Aim for about 450 whitespace-separated words in total.

primary: exact-model accuracy on all held-out prompts
baseline: fixed C=1 logistic regression; no test tuning; 12 and 60 training examples
order_check: GPT zero-shot, all 40 items with reversed candidate order
single_check: GPT zero-shot, four explain-4 outputs individually
note: 10 test prompt clusters; descriptive secondary comparisons; no claim about unseen source models
